claim: For an ordinary smooth genus-two curve \(X\) over an algebraically closed field \(k\) of characteristic \(2\), the scheme-theoretic base locus of the Frobenius-pullback (Verschiebung) map \(V:\mathcal M_{X_1}\dashrightarrow\mathcal M_X\) on moduli spaces of semistable rank-two bundles with trivial determinant is supported at \((1:1:1:1)\) in theta coordinates and has local ring \(k[a,b]/(a^2,b^2)\); in particular, it is a length-\(4\) local complete intersection with Hilbert function \((1,2,1)\).

correctness.rationale: The coordinate equations reduce to the local ideal \((c+a+b+ab,a^2,b^2)\); eliminating c gives \(k[a,b]/(a^2,b^2)\), with basis \(1,a,b,ab\) and length \(4\). The equations also imply unique geometric support at \((1:1:1:1)\).

evidence: Lange–Pauly's theorem states genus two, ordinary, and \(p>2\); it does not include \(p=2\).
Osserman's accessible abstract states the genus-two degree computation in characteristic \(p>2\).
Laszlo–Pauly's 2002 paper treats a nonordinary characteristic-two case and characteristic three; its sixteen-point base locus is a different case.
broader_coverage.reasoning: No inspected theorem has hypotheses that cover ordinary genus two in characteristic two and assert the local base-ring type. The \(p>2\) length formula numerically specializes to four, but its theorem cannot be applied outside its stated hypotheses and does not supply this local algebra.

value.rationale: The scheme structure of an indeterminacy locus is a natural local invariant controlling its resolution. The ordinary characteristic-two case is excluded from the published \(p>2\) scheme-theoretic theorem; the length-four complete-intersection type provides the local center and infinitesimal structure, beyond the already-known single support point.
